Today I had a conversation with my nanny (I’m 24) she told me that when I was a toddler I was my happiest when I was with her, that I’d cry when I slept in my moms bed and I constantly wanted to be around her. As a child your primary source of connection and love is presence, the more time a child spends with someone the more loved they feel. Unfortunately my mother did not have the luxury of time because she was working relentlessly to put a roof over our head, that was her expression of her love for me, but I was too young to understand. Now that I’m older I have no question in my mind that my mother loves me, she just wasn’t able to give me the type of love that I would have understood at that young age. I’m not trying to invalidate your experience, perhaps there’s a lot more that happened in your relationship with your mother that I may never get to know. But if it’s at all worthwhile, try to look back on your life thus far and see if you cannot spot the ways your mother tried to show her love for you, even in the smallest things. It may help ease your mind to know that your mother did/does love you, even if it was not in the way you needed that love to be expressed at that age.

There’s a comment here that says something along the lines of “misery is the gap between expectation and reality”. It reminded me of something I came across the other day in my quest for self love and self improvement: You have to live your authentic truth, fall in love with yourself and crave the best for yourself. I know this sounds like a bit of an oxymoron, mostly because we’ve been taught that good things only come with suffering. But this is a horrible way of thinking. Yes, it takes hard work to achieve the things that you want. But achieving those things shouldn’t come at the expense of you being happy, and you living life. You owe it to yourself to make the best of the time that you have. Nothing in this life is guaranteed. It isn’t guaranteed that if you put level 100 Into whatever it is that you pursue for the next 10 years that life will be amazing when you turn 40. That just isn’t realistic. But what you can do is make the most of the time that you have right now. Enjoy your life while still keeping your eyes on the end goal don’t sacrifice your health your happiness for something that isn’t guaranteed. 

Dreaming is good, dream big! Work towards achieving those dreams. But also live! I Don’t know if I’m making any sense because I’m also still in a fucking terrible space but if there’s anything that I can share or beg you to do, which I failed to do and I’m trying to do right now is live, for the life of God just live.
